title: TIMI Risk Score for STEMI
keywords: distinguish from the existing TIMI NSTEMI score already in Kairos
sources: Morrow DA, et al. TIMI Risk Score for ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction: A Convenient, Bedside, Clinical Score for Risk Assessment at Presentation. Circulation. 2000;102(17):2031-2037.

changelog.change: Initial entry — a genuine content gap (Content audit 2026-09-14, Batch 3). Kairos already had the TIMI score for NSTEMI/UA (a different score, different variables); this is the distinct STEMI-specific version. Point values WebSearch-verified against the original 2000 Circulation derivation paper.

purpose: 30-day mortality risk estimate at presentation for STEMI, using variables available immediately at the bedside — distinct from the TIMI NSTEMI/UA score already in Kairos, which uses different criteria entirely.
notes: A different tool from the existing TIMI (NSTEMI/UA) score — do not conflate the two despite the shared name; this one was derived specifically in fibrinolytic-era STEMI patients and uses Killip class, weight, and time-to-treatment rather than the NSTEMI score's aspirin-use/prior-stenosis/recent-angina criteria.

items.label: History of diabetes, hypertension, or angina (any one)
Anterior ST elevation, or new left bundle branch block
Time from symptom onset to treatment

interpretation.label: Score 8+
interpretation.detail: ≈ 26.8-35.9% 30-day mortality — steep, near-linear climb per point at the top of the range.

buildNote: Mortality percentages are the point-by-point figures from the original Morrow 2000 derivation cohort (fibrinolytic-era), reproduced as commonly cited — treat as an order-of-magnitude risk gradient rather than a precise modern-era number, since contemporary primary-PCI mortality is generally lower across the board. The score itself (which variables, how many points each) is the durable, still-used part; the raw percentages are the part most likely to have drifted from a 2000-era fibrinolytic cohort. Distinct calculator from the existing TIMI NSTEMI/UA score — cross-link via aliases/keywords since calculator schema has no related[] field.
